messages:
maria_support: FYI - getting multiple reports from EU enterprise customers about p95/p99 spikes and intermittent 500s during the 02:00-02:15 UTC billing window burst. Appears tied to scale-up events to Dedicated pools.

rachel_support: Seeing 3 separate tickets in the last 12m. All describe ~20-30s tail latencies and occasional auth 500s for short periods. Attaching one repro from customer A: they sent a 1k qps burst for 30s.

maria_support: Repro curl (customer traffic simulator):
```bash
for i in {1..1000}; do curl -sS -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate & done; wait
```
Response pattern: tokens stream then 500s start to appear, backend logs show "attach timeout=30s" and queue growth.

sam_oncall: @jin_sre @alex_platform can you grab attach logs + metrics for the EU-dedicated pool 7 during that window? Also need request IDs and any auth proxy 5xx.

deploy-bot: Scale policy change applied to pool-7: min_replicas=2 -> 4, applied by ops at 2026-02-14T01:58:40Z.

jin_sre: Pulling logs now. Early notes: attach latency spikes correlate with high concurrent attach attempts after bursts. We see a mix of cold GPU init time and container image pull stalls (~8-12s) + model cache init (~10-18s) for larger models. Also observed auth-proxy returning 502s when upstream backend queue length > 500.

alex_platform: Kernel image pull times for that region spiked due to registry throttling; we have a mitigation in train (requesting larger burst rate from registry partner), but short term we can increase local image cache TTL and prefetch for heavy pools.

sam_oncall: Two immediate mitigations to reduce customer impact: 1) raise min_ready_replicas for busy dedicated pools in EU to 4 (deploy-bot already applied to pool-7), 2) lower attach timeout on control plane from 30s -> 20s to fail fast and trigger fallback path (hot-attach fallback to warm cache). Thoughts?

jin_sre: Lowering attach timeout will reduce auth 500s surface but could increase attach failures; need to enable fallback logic before tightening timeout. Propose: enable fallback-model-variant (smaller quantized model) for heavy traffic customers + enable prefix KV cache warmup.

rachel_support: Can we also apply customer-side rate limiting for the most aggressive tenants while we stabilize? I can push temporary rate-limit flags per-account to avoid cascade.

alex_platform: Agree. Immediate action plan:
- Increase min_ready_replicas for EU dedicated pools to 4 for top 10 tenants (ops rollout done for pool-7).
- Enable image prefetch + raise local registry burst (in-progress with infra partner).
- Flip on fallback-model-variant for elite customers hitting p99 > 5s.
- Deploy a control-plane flag to reduce attach timeout from 30s -> 20s simultaneous with fallback enablement.

sam_oncall: I'll own the timeout flip and monitoring. Jin, can you own the fallback rollout and KV warmup script? Maria/Rachel, please notify affected customers of temporary rate limits and mitigations.

jin_sre: Taking fallback rollout. I'll also add extra logging for attach path: request_id, pool_id, attach_duration_ms, image_pull_ms, cache_init_ms. Patch will be rolled to staging then canary EU pool in ~45m.

maria_support: Notifying customers now with summary + mitigation ETA ~1h. Sample message: "We're proactively increasing pool warm capacity and enabling a fallback model variant to reduce latency during bursts. We'll follow up with post-incident notes." :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: fallback-variant=true on pool-7-canary at 2026-02-14T02:10:12Z.

rachel_support: Tickets updated with action items and links to canary dashboard. Marking P1 for tracking.

sam_oncall: Monitoring live metrics. If p99 doesn't drop after canary + min_ready increase, we'll schedule a short rolling restart to force image cache repopulation on remaining nodes.

jin_sre: Added temporary alert: EU-dedicated-pool attach_errors > 5/min -> paging. Also created internal issue INF-4721 to track root causes (registry throttling + cache warm behavior).

maria_support: Thanks team. I'll circle back in 45m with customer updates.

sam_oncall: Update 20m later: canary shows p99 reduced from ~28s -> ~3.5s and attach error rate dropped 90%. Leaving mitigations in place for 2h and will revisit.

maria_support: Customers confirmed much improved latencies. Closing immediate escalation, keeping postmortem in eng-sre.

jin_sre: Postmortem stub created, will add full timeline, metrics, and long-term mitigation proposals (proactive warmup schedules, registry QoS, model size nudging) by EOD.

rachel_support: Closing support tickets as resolved, follow-up notes added. Thanks everyone.
